summary.headline: POWERGRID Q1 FY27 PAT flat at Rs 3,598 crore (vs Rs 3,631 crore QoQ) as regulatory drag of ~Rs 560 crore offset Rs 790 crore transmission-charge growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated transmission charges rose 3% QoQ to Rs 10,905 crore and total income to Rs 11,697 crore, but PAT was Rs 3,598 crore against Rs 3,631 crore in the prior quarter. Management attributed the flat profit to a ~Rs 560 crore regulatory drag: Rs 330 crore lower depreciation/interest recovery and Rs 230 crore of interest on provisional-vs-final tariff differential that is no longer available, plus a Rs 33 crore one-off write-back (KSK Mahanadi) in the base quarter. Capitalisation of Rs 5,277 crore in Q1 was about 3.1x the prior-year Q1 figure of Rs 1,683 crore, against a FY27 guidance of Rs 30,000 crore. Receivable days fell to about 12 from 19.41, with Rs 11,404 crore realised against Rs 10,963 crore billed.

segments.name: Transmission (regulated RTM and TBCB)
segments.commentary: Transmission charges up Rs 790 crore from new assets, offset by regulatory drag of ~Rs 560 crore; TBCB operational equity investment rose to Rs 9,965 crore from Rs 4,671 crore a year earlier, funded through internal accruals.

segments.name: Consultancy
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 252 crore; 16 domestic and 3 international orders, footprint in about 25 countries.

segments.name: Telecom (PowerTel)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 391 crore; connectivity extended to Andaman and Nicobar and first international link to Nepal; 100% backbone availability claimed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guidance Rs 37,000 crore; management says Q1 capex already more than 10% of the annual guidance... as stated on call, capex is more than 10% of guidance achieved in Q1 itself.
FY27 capitalisation guidance Rs 30,000 crore; Q1 at Rs 5,277 crore, with Koppal, Gadag and Bidar-Maheshwaram projects expected to be commissioned later.
Rs 300 crore of RTM revenue pending CERC deemed-DOCO orders, to accrue as regulator hears petitions.
Works in hand about Rs 1.75 lakh crore (TBCB Rs 1.46 lakh crore, RTM Rs 25,000 crore, others Rs 4,200 crore); bidding pipeline Rs 1.19 lakh crore; long-term outlook above Rs 15 lakh crore.
Estimated Rs 7.9 lakh crore of transmission capex to 2035-36 expected to be bid over the next 3-4 years; estimate excludes land compensation under new MoP guidelines.
risks_watch: Regulatory drag from ageing 2014-16 capitalisation and CERC order timing: Rs 560 crore in Q1 with further depreciation step-ups expected as assets mature past 12 years.
Capitalisation run-rate: Rs 5,277 crore in Q1 against Rs 30,000 crore FY27 guidance requires heavy back-ended commissioning dependent on RoW and land compensation.
Land compensation under new MoP guidelines is not in the Rs 7.9 lakh crore estimate and may raise costs; state adoption still settling.
Limited disclosure: management declined a separate TBCB consolidated P&L, drawing analyst pushback; the company will examine better disclosures.
Equipment supply and raw-material cost risk for transformers and GIS; Chinese OEM participation is a changing variable.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, capex and capitalisation, but defensive and repeatedly stressing the regulatory drag when pressed on flat PAT and TBCB disclosure. Evasive on specifics such as Barmer HVDC award date, BESS timing and the normative versus actual debt gap, promising follow-ups.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the regulatory drag in depreciation and revenue this quarter, and how will it evolve as 2014-16 assets age?
qa_highlights.answer: Management quantified the drag at about Rs 560 crore for Q1: Rs 330 crore depreciation/interest and Rs 230 crore interest on the CERC differential. It said assets capitalised about 12 years ago will continue to weigh, and framed this as part of the regulatory characteristic.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT flat if the change is profit-neutral, and what is the adjusted base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 230 crore interest on the provisional-vs-final differential is no longer available and a Rs 33 crore write-back (KSK Mahanadi) in the prior quarter does not recur. It said the regulatory differential is the major factor, with a small depreciation/interest mismatch versus notional figures.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Rs 13,000 crore TBCB equity funded, and what is the Rs 7.9 lakh crore transmission capex timeline and land cost treatment?
qa_highlights.answer: All TBCB equity is funded from internal accruals with no parent-level debt. Management said the Rs 7.9 lakh crore to 2035-36 would be bid over the next 3-4 years and excludes land compensation under new MoP guidelines, which Delhi, Haryana and Gujarat have adopted.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Barmer HVDC award and BESS opportunity under the regulated route?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bids for the Rajasthan Phase IV Barmer Complex HVDC are submitted and under evaluation by the bid process coordinator, with no award date yet. On BESS, it said petitions have been filed before the regulator after NR and WR RPC consent, with timing dependent on regulator and stakeholder positions.

qa_highlights.question: Can TBCB consolidated revenue, EBITDA and PAT be disclosed separately, and what returns are earned on operational TBCB equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a separate TBCB P&L or return figure. It said returns are calibrated across multiple projects and that it will examine better disclosures, while noting regulatory disclosures are already made.

qa_highlights.question: Is there scope for upside to the Rs 30,000 crore capitalisation guidance, and why is the gross block-to-depreciation gap so wide?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transmission capitalisation follows project timelines and ROW constraints, citing Rs 5,277 crore in Q1 and Koppal, Gadag and Bidar-Maheshwaram to follow. On the gap, management said TBCB projects are under the lease accounting method, so depreciation is replaced by lease amortisation, and PAT is unaffected by the method.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance Rs 37,000 crore; management said Q1 capex already exceeds 10% of that guidance.

Q1 FY27 commissioning: about 1,635 ckm of transmission lines (about 35% of Q1 FY26 achievement) and about 10,500 MVA of transformation capacity; lines include 765 kV Kurnool III-Maheshwaram, 765 kV Dausa-Beawar, 400 kV Navsari-Kala and 400 kV Kadapa-Anantapur.
Post-June 2026 completions: 765 kV Raichur-Koppal II PS, 400 kV Gadag II-Koppal II PS, 400 kV Bikaner II and Bikaner III, and a new 765/400 kV Koppal substation; mostly linked to RE evacuation.
Capitalisation Rs 5,277 crore in Q1 vs Rs 1,683 crore in Q1 FY26, about 3.13x; FY27 guidance Rs 30,000 crore. Koppal, Gadag and Bidar-Maheshwaram expected to be capitalised later.

Works in hand about Rs 1.75 lakh crore (TBCB Rs 1.46 lakh crore, RTM about Rs 25,000 crore, others about Rs 4,200 crore incl. smart metering, data centre, BESS), of which about Rs 50,000 crore is CWIP; bidding pipeline Rs 1.19 lakh crore; TBCB wins till July 2026: 6 projects of 19 bid, gross annual tariff about Rs 2,200 crore; first synchronous condenser project won (two at Fatehgarh II).
demand_pricing: Transmission charges up Rs 790 crore QoQ-equivalent from new assets; ~Rs 247 crore PAT uplift from new assets, offset by ~Rs 560 crore regulatory drag (Rs 330 crore lower depreciation/interest recovery, Rs 230 crore lower interest on provisional-vs-final tariff differential).
Tariff is recovered per annum (Rs per annum, not Rs per MWh), so revenue is not linked to power flow; management says generation delays affect revenue only if the generator or load is late.
Rs 300 crore of RTM revenue pending CERC deemed-DOCO orders, to accrue as the regulator hears petitions.
Billing Rs 10,963 crore vs realisation Rs 11,404 crore (~104%); receivable days down from 19.41 to about 12.

Equipment: bulk procurement initiative with OEMs; management says transformer prices are stabilising but raw material costs continue to weigh; four Chinese companies recently allowed by GoI, POWERGRID to comply with guidelines.
Consultancy revenue Rs 252 crore (16 domestic, 3 international orders, ~25 countries); telecom (PowerTel) revenue Rs 391 crore.
